criteria.text: The response identifies that the Supply Agreement's exclusivity obligation requires Leilisk to buy all Glass Products exclusively from Seineix for projects anywhere in North America, far broader than the term sheet's exclusivity limited to triple-silver low-E IGUs for New York, New Jersey and Connecticut projects. It locates this in the Supply Agreement (Section 3.1), explains why this matters to Leilisk, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Quality Agreement's narrow definition of 'Defect' (deviations detectable by visual inspection at the time of Delivery) controls over the Supply Agreement's broader definition. As a result, the 10-year IGU warranty is cut down to defects visible at Delivery and no longer covers latent seal failure, coating degradation or nickel-sulfide breakage. It locates this in the Quality Agreement (Section 1.4) or the Supply Agreement (Section 21.2), explains why this matters to Leilisk, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Supply Agreement renews automatically for successive 60-month Renewal Terms unless Leilisk gives non-renewal notice within a ten-business-day Opt-Out Period ending about 180 days before the end of the term. It locates this in the Supply Agreement (Section 2.2) or the Order Form (Section 2), explains why this matters to Leilisk, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Leilisk's pending acquisition by Ostrander Building Group is a Change of Control requiring Seineix's prior written consent, and that nothing in the documents shows this consent has been obtained. It locates this in the Supply Agreement (Section 16.2) or the Order Form (Section 6), explains why this matters to Leilisk, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Leilisk's 30-day window to object to the Price Adjustment Notice received on March 4, 2026 closed in early April 2026. It concludes that the April 20, 2026 objection letter was untimely, so Seineix can treat the price increase as deemed accepted. It locates this in the Supply Agreement (Section 5.3) or the Order Form (Section 3), explains why this matters to Leilisk, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Supply Agreement imposes a minimum annual purchase commitment of 400,000 square feet of Glass Products per Contract Year.
The response states that the Supply Agreement's Initial Term is 60 months (five years) from the Effective Date.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it sets out where the issue appears (document and section), why it matters for Leilisk, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that Leilisk's April 20, 2026 objection to the price adjustment was made within the Supply Agreement's objection period.
The response claims that the October 2023 term sheet's narrower exclusivity scope binds Seineix and limits the Supply Agreement's exclusivity clause.
